title: Strict tower homotopy limit
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$, whose objects are strict inverse sequences and whose exactness is levelwise. On its derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], total right derived inverse limit is computed by taking a K-injective tower resolution and then termwise inverse limit [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. This gives an exact functor $R\lim:D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))\to D(\mathcal A)$. For every strict tower complex $X_\bullet$ there is a natural distinguished triangle $R\lim X_\bullet\to\prod_n^D X_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_n^D X_n\to(R\lim X_\bullet)[1]$ [def-weil-derived-limit], where $\prod^D$ is the product in $D(\mathcal A)$ and the $n$-th component of $s$ is transition followed by projection to $n+1$. In particular, if for every $n$ some transition $X_m\to X_n$, $m\geq n$, is zero in $D(\mathcal A)$, then $R\lim X_\bullet=0$. If $v:X_\bullet\to Y_\bullet$ is a strict map of tower complexes whose tower of mapping cones has that property, then the canonical map $R\lim(v)$ is an isomorphism. No exactness of countable products in $\mathcal A$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), in particular Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); the proof works for modules using the constant pullback ring sheaf on the tower site. Pro-zero consequence: the finite geometric-series inverse of 1-s, or Tag 0H9L (more-algebra-lemma-pro-isomorphism-Rlim) in more-algebra.tex, applied to the zero tower. Strict functoriality uses the total derived functor on the tower site.

proof.text: Give $\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\geq1}$ the arrows $(U,n)\to(V,m)$ equal to arrows $U\to V$ when $n\leq m$, and none otherwise; coverings are precisely the coverings in $\mathcal C$ at a fixed index. Put $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{tow}}(U,n)=\mathcal O(U)$. The sheaf condition is the sheaf condition separately at each index, and restriction along $(U,n)\to(U,n+1)$ supplies the tower transition. Thus sheaves of $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{tow}}$-modules are exactly strict towers of $\mathcal O$-modules, including their morphisms. The tower site is small and its coefficient sheaf is commutative. Apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on this site to obtain a functorial K-injective resolution $X_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ with injective terms. The tower category and its evaluations are abelian and exact by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Inverse limit is additive and is right adjoint to the exact constant-tower functor: a map from a constant tower to $T_\bullet$ is precisely a compatible family of maps into $T_n$. Termwise inverse limit commutes with shifts and mapping cones, since it commutes with finite biproducts; it preserves chain homotopies by applying inverse limit to the homotopy equations. Consequently it defines an exact functor $K(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))\to D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to obtain its total right derived functor, computed by $Q(\varprojlim I_n)$. This is an exact functor by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. The formula holds for every K-injective tower representative: [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identifies two such representatives by a unique homotopy class of homotopy equivalences, and additive inverse limit preserves that equivalence.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits); Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), first proof paragraph; derived.tex Tags 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies) and 070I (lemma-K-injective).

proof.text: Each evaluated complex $I_n$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective]. Products of module sheaves exist sectionwise: $P(U)=\prod_n F_n(U)$ with coordinatewise restrictions and module action is a sheaf, because a matching family glues uniquely in each coordinate. Hence [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective], whose statement is for any abelian category, shows that $P=\prod_n I_n$ represents $\prod_n^D X_n$. For an injective tower object $J$, let $T_n(F)$ be $F$ at indices $1,\ldots,n$, with identity transitions there, and zero above $n$. Maps $T_n(F)\to J$ correspond to maps $F\to J_n$. The natural inclusion $T_n(F)\hookrightarrow T_{n+1}(F)$ is monic by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. By the definition of injectivity [def-sp-injective-resolutions], with $F=J_n$, the map corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_{J_n}$ extends across this inclusion, giving a section $\sigma_n:J_n\to J_{n+1}$ of the transition $q_n:J_{n+1}\to J_n$. Apply this to $J=I^r_\bullet$ in each degree $r$. For sections $x=(x_n)$ of $P^r$ over any $U$, set $y_1=0$ and recursively $y_{n+1}=\sigma_n(y_n-x_n)$. Then $y_n-q_n y_{n+1}=x_n$, so $1-s:P^r\to P^r$ is surjective on sections. Its kernel is exactly the compatible-sequence sheaf $L^r=\varprojlim_n I_n^r$. Thus $0\to L\to P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\to0$ is degreewise short exact. The natural triangle of this short exact sequence is distinguished by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]; its first vertex is $R\lim X_\bullet$ by Step 1 and its middle vertices are the derived products just established.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), proof: injective transitions, exact left adjoint to evaluation, and the short exact product sequence; derived.tex Tag 0BK6 (lemma-product-K-injective).

proof.text: The middle arrow of Step 2 satisfies $\mathrm{pr}_n(1-s)=\mathrm{pr}_n-q_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$, which is precisely the endomorphism of [def-weil-derived-limit]. For a strict chain map $v:X_\bullet\to Y_\bullet$, use the functorial tower-site resolutions of Step 1 to obtain $I(v):I(X)_\bullet\to I(Y)_\bullet$. The tower-map equation $I(v)_n q_n=q'_n I(v)_{n+1}$ gives $(\prod_n I(v)_n)(1-s)=(1-s')(\prod_n I(v)_n)$ after every projection. The restriction of this product map to compatible sequences is $\varprojlim I(v)_n$. These three maps form a morphism of the short exact sequences in Step 2, so their localized maps, including the connecting arrows, form a morphism of distinguished triangles by the naturality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. Its first map is the canonical $R\lim(v)$ of Step 1. For morphisms in the derived tower category, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents them by unique homotopy classes between K-injective towers; the displayed construction respects homotopies and therefore is natural on that category. This proves the asserted natural Roos triangle without choosing a nonunique map between unrelated homotopy limits.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits) and Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); natural short-exact-sequence triangle, derived.tex Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor).

proof.text: Suppose the evaluated tower is pro-zero in $D(\mathcal A)$. Write $P=\prod_n^D X_n$ and $s:P\to P$ for its shift endomorphism. For each $n$ choose $r_n\geq1$ such that $\mathrm{pr}_n s^{r_n}=0$: a zero transition $X_m\to X_n$ gives $r_n=m-n$ when $m>n$, and if $m=n$ then $X_n=0$ and take $r_n=1$. Define $t:P\to P$ by $\mathrm{pr}_n t=\sum_{k=0}^{r_n-1}\mathrm{pr}_n s^k$, using the product universal property [def-weil-category-product]. All later summands vanish, so these finite sums are unchanged upon increasing $r_n$. Telescoping gives $\mathrm{pr}_n t(1-s)=\mathrm{pr}_n$. Also $f_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}t=\sum_{k=1}^{r_{n+1}}\mathrm{pr}_n s^k=\sum_{k\geq1}\mathrm{pr}_n s^k$ (a finite sum), since $\mathrm{pr}_n s^{r_{n+1}+1}=f_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}s^{r_{n+1}}=0$. Hence $\mathrm{pr}_n(1-s)t=\mathrm{pr}_n$, and $t$ is a two-sided inverse of $1-s$. In the Roos triangle $H\xrightarrow{p}P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\xrightarrow{\delta}H[1]$, consecutive composites are zero [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact], so $p=0$ and $\delta=0$ because $1-s$ is invertible. Rotate the triangle backwards [def-weil-triangulated-category] to $P[-1]\xrightarrow{-\delta[-1]}H\xrightarrow{p}P\to P$. Exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}(H,-)$ at $H$ [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] factors $\mathrm{id}_H$ through $-\delta[-1]=0$. Thus $\mathrm{id}_H=0$ and $H=R\lim X_\bullet$ is a zero object. This is a coordinatewise finite calculation, requiring no uniform nilpotence bound or exactness of products.

source.place: Tag 0H9L (lemma-pro-isomorphism-Rlim), pro-zero case; explicit finite-series calculation in the Roos triangle of derived.tex Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit).

proof.text: For a strict chain map $v:X_\bullet\to Y_\bullet$, its mapping cone $C(v)$ is formed in the tower category; evaluation gives $C(v)_n=C(v_n)$ by the degreewise biproduct-and-differential formula [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The cone triangle $X_\bullet\xrightarrow{v}Y_\bullet\to C(v)\to X_\bullet[1]$ is distinguished. Exactness of $R\lim$ from Step 1, supplied by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated], gives a distinguished triangle whose first arrow is the canonical $u=R\lim(v)$. Under the hypothesis on the cone tower, Step 4 makes its third vertex zero. Put $A=R\lim X_\bullet$ and $B=R\lim Y_\bullet$. Exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}(B,-)$ in $A\xrightarrow{u}B\to0\to A[1]$ [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] gives $r:B\to A$ with $ur=\mathrm{id}_B$. Apply the same exactness statement to the backwards rotated triangle $0[-1]\to A\xrightarrow{u}B\to0$ [def-weil-triangulated-category]: $u(ru-\mathrm{id}_A)=0$ implies that $ru-\mathrm{id}_A$ factors through $0[-1]$, so it is zero. Therefore $r$ is a two-sided inverse and the canonical $R\lim(v)$ is an isomorphism.

theorem ringedStrictTowerHomotopyLimitOfUniverses
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max uC vC r}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max uC vC r}]
    (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{max uC vC r})
    (_hcomm : ∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (a b : R.obj.obj U), a * b = b * a)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r, max uC vC r, vC, uC} R)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r, max uC vC r, vC, uC} R)] :
    ∃ (RF : DerivedCategory.{w}
        (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r, max uC vC r, vC, uC} R) ⥤
      DerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r, max uC vC r, vC, uC} R))
      (η : (lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r, max uC vC r, vC, uC} R) ⥤
        ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r, max uC vC r, vC, uC} R).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q.{w} ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.{w} ⋙ RF),
      RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor η
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso
          (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r, max uC vC r, vC, uC} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ I, CochainComplex.IsKInjective I → IsIso (η.app I)) ∧
      (∀ (X : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r, max uC vC r, vC, uC} R) ℤ),
        ∃ (I : CochainComplex
          (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r, max uC vC r, vC, uC} R) ℤ) (j : X ⟶ I),
          I.IsKInjective ∧ QuasiIso j) ∧
      ∃ (_hshift : RF.CommShift ℤ)
        (_hproducts : HasCountableProducts
          (DerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r, max uC vC r, vC, uC} R)))
        (E : DerivedCategory.{w}
          (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r, max uC vC r, vC, uC} R) ⥤
            (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory.{w}
              (ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r, max uC vC r, vC, uC} R)))
        (_ε : DerivedCategory.Q.{w} ⋙ E ≅
          HomologicalComplex.complexOfFunctorsToFunctorToComplex ⋙
            (Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ
              (CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r, max uC vC r, vC, uC} R) ℤ)
              (DerivedCategory.{w}
                (ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r, max uC vC r, vC, uC} R))).obj
                  DerivedCategory.Q.{w})
        (p : ∀ Z,
          RF.obj Z ⟶ ∏ᶜ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (E.obj Z).obj (op n)))
        (δ : ∀ Z,
          (∏ᶜ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (E.obj Z).obj (op n))) ⟶ (RF.obj Z)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
        RF.IsTriangulated ∧
        (∀ Z,
          IsDerivedLimitTriangle
            (fun n : ℕ ↦ (E.obj Z).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op)
            (RF.obj Z) (p Z) (δ Z)) ∧
        (∀ {Z W} (v : Z ⟶ W),
          RF.map v ≫ p W = p Z ≫ Limits.Pi.map (fun n : ℕ ↦ (E.map v).app (op n))) ∧
        (∀ {Z W} (v : Z ⟶ W),
          Limits.Pi.map (fun n : ℕ ↦ (E.map v).app (op n)) ≫ δ W =
            δ Z ≫ (RF.map v)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧') ∧
        (∀ Z,
          (∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (m : ℕ) (h : n ≤ m), (E.obj Z).map (homOfLE h).op = 0) →
            IsZero (RF.obj Z)) ∧
        (∀ (X Y : CochainComplex
          (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r, max uC vC r, vC, uC} R) ℤ) (v : X ⟶ Y),
          (∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (m : ℕ) (h : n ≤ m),
            (E.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj (CochainComplex.mappingCone v))).map
              (homOfLE h).op = 0) → IsIso (RF.map (DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.map v)))
